primary_meaning: False believers, hypocrites, or 'sons of the evil one' who coexist alongside true believers in the world or the visible church until the final judgment.

alternatives.meaning: Heretics and false teachers who introduce corrupt doctrines into the church.
Sinful tendencies, vices, or evil thoughts growing alongside virtues within an individual believer's soul.

notes: Because the Gospel of Matthew includes an explicit interpretation attributed to Jesus (Matthew 13:38), there is overwhelming consensus that tares represent children of the evil one. Historical debates primarily revolve around ecclesiology, specifically whether the field is strictly the world or the visible church, rather than the symbolic definition of the tares themselves.
